District governance: Audible upgrades bring safer streets
body:
Many pedestrians in Hong Kong might barely notice the steady rhythm of the “yellow box” mounted on traffic lights, but for a visually impaired resident like Lee Kai-tak, that sound is a lifeline.

 

The “yellow box” is the electronic audible traffic signal (eATS), which utilises sound and vibrations to alert visually impaired people to changes in pedestrian lights.

 

While most of the original eATS have been in operation for more than two decades, the Transport Department has been progressively rolling out a new generation of devices across the city since April 2025, adding a range of people-oriented features.

 

As of August this year, more than 800 pedestrian crossings have been upgraded with new devices, accounting for 40% of the city’s total.

 

Thoughtful features

Having lost his sight more than 30 years ago, 57-year-old Mr Lee is a passionate advocate. His schedule is packed as he travels extensively across Hong Kong Island, Kowloon and the New Territories for government and organisational meetings.

As someone who usually goes out alone, he relies heavily on these audible devices to navigate the streets.

 

The upgrade introduces several features designed to make daily travel easier. The one Mr Lee relies on most is the voice message at crossing locations, which reads out street names in Cantonese, Putonghua and English.

 

“It is indispensable,” Mr Lee said. “When I am heading somewhere I do not know very well, I need to know which street I am on.”

 

The tactile map on the device is another key addition, helping visually impaired people get a sense of road layouts.

 

Taking Hong Kong Island as an example, Mr Lee noted that the district possesses ordinary traffic lanes alongside tram tracks and mixed traffic sections shared by cars and trams. Before crossing, understanding the terrain is crucial.

 

Mr Lee believes that safe, comprehensive and reliable accessibility features are vital in helping visually impaired individuals integrate into the community and build a new life.

 

“Just imagine - a visually impaired person steps out of their building, and the first thing they have to do is to cross the road," he said. "But if we dread stepping off the kerb, with nothing to help us, where do we find the courage to face a new life?”

 

Fortunately, all crossings in Hong Kong are equipped with audible devices - something Mr Lee notes only a handful of cities worldwide can claim, making him proud of the city’s progress.

 

He is also satisfied with the pace of the replacement, especially as the department prioritises areas near organisations for the visually impaired.

 

User-driven design

As a long-time user, Mr Lee is not just benefiting from the new devices - he helped design them.

 

Collaborating closely with the department since it began exploring improvements in 2017, he and his peers inspired many of the new features.

 

While the new devices lower the volume at night to reduce disturbance to nearby residents, extra assistance is required if a visually impaired person needs to cross after dark.

 

Following discussions with Mr Lee, the department introduced a dedicated remote control and a mobile application for volume adjustments.

 

A total of 15,000 dedicated remote controls are being distributed by the Government through organisations for the visually impaired.

 

The remote is simple in design. The “1” button gives the audible signal a one-off volume boost, while the round “O” button keeps raising the volume on a loop for 20 minutes.

 

Mr Lee described it as a “ten-out-of-ten design” and praised the department for fully embracing the views of the community.

 

Making progress

“Ensuring road safety and improving pedestrian facilities are key aspects of the Government’s district governance measures,” said Transport Department Chief Engineer (Traffic Control) Gordon Kwok.

 

Mr Kwok described the replacement as progressing as intended, and expects the target of completing updates at about 2,000 junctions across Hong Kong will be met by late 2027.

 

He noted that the department prioritises areas where visually impaired people frequently pass by, such as Sham Shui Po and Kwun Tong.

 

Highlighting the new flexible volume control function, Mr Kwok explained that lowering the night-time sound levels of the devices by up to 5 decibels cuts resident disturbance, while the remote control or mobile application ensures safety when needed.

 

“This is a win-win arrangement that precisely addresses public needs, while fostering a more harmonious and inclusive society,” he said.

title: San Tin land to be resumed
body:
The Lands Department today posted land resumption notices for the third batch of Phase 1 and the first batch of Phase 2 of the San Tin Technopole (STT) development, alongside acquisition notices for the Phase 2 development.

 

Under the Lands Resumption Ordinance, a total of eight private lots, covering an area of about 0.3 hectares, will be resumed for the third batch of Phase 1 development.

 

Furthermore, a total of 1,043 private lots, covering an area of about 44.2 hectares, will be resumed for the first batch of Phase 2 development.

 

In addition, government land occupied by 67 graves and 148 urns, covering an area of about 1,985 sq m, as well as land occupied by two fishponds totalling 325 sq m, will be acquired under the Land Acquisition (Possessory Title) Ordinance.

 

All of the land will officially revert to the Government on December 26.

 

The department will post notices in relevant areas about three months before the departure deadlines for the affected parties, estimating that those affected by both the third batch of Phase 1 and the first batch of Phase 2 development will need to move out starting from the first quarter of 2027.

 

The STT project spans a total area of approximately 540 hectares and is being rolled out in two phases, with Stage 1 works having commenced at the end of 2024.

 

Upon its full operation, the project is expected to provide over 300,000 full-time jobs for the Hong Kong economy as a whole.

 

The first batch of residents under the Phase 1 development will start moving in progressively from 2031.

title: FS meets financial leaders in Qatar
body:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan met various financial leaders as he began a visit to Doha, Qatar.

 

On his first day in the country, Mr Chan met Qatar's Minister of Finance H.E. Ali bin Ahmed Al Kuwari to exchange views on various topics, such as strengthening co-operation between Hong Kong and Qatar.

 

After the meeting, Mr Chan held in-depth exchanges with local business leaders from various sectors. He briefed them on Hong Kong's strengths and invited Qatari enterprises and investors to participate in the development of the Northern Metropolis.

 

The finance chief also met President and Chair of the Board of Directors of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) Zou Jiayi.

 

Mr Chan commended the AIIB's establishment of an office in Hong Kong and said he looked forward to expanding co-operation with it in areas such as catastrophe bond issuance, green finance, technology and innovation, and talent training.

 

Throughout the day, Mr Chan met a number of political, business and financial leaders, including Doha Venture Capital's Chief Executive Officer Mohammed Al-Abdulla and Chief Financial Officer Niall Byrne; Qatar Investment Authority Chief of Investment Execution Ken McLaren; and the senior management of Lesha Bank Group and Al Asmakh Group Holding.

 

In the evening, Mr Chan attended the AIIB President's Reception, hosted by Ms Zou, where he exchanged views with representatives from several governments, multilateral development organisations, businesses and financial institutions.

 

Mr Chan will continue his itinerary in Doha today, attending events related to the AIIB Annual Meeting, before departing for Hong Kong late into the night.

title: FS visits CICC in Beijing
body:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan visited China International Capital Corporation Limited (CICC) in Beijing today and met with its Chairman Chen Liang. They had in-depth talks on securities markets, renminbi internationalisation, financial infrastructure and mutual market access.

 

Mr Chan said that building China into a financial powerhouse requires strong international financial centres and institutions. He noted that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government's recently announced First Five-Year Plan and the 2026 Policy Address focus on strengthening Hong Kong's role as a top financial hub.

 

These plans support quality enterprises using Hong Kong to grow, serve the real economy, and boost the innovation and technology sector.

 

Mr Chan expressed hope that CICC will maintain close ties with Hong Kong's financial regulators to help the city’s capital markets and grow its international business, especially in Belt & Road countries. By leveraging Hong Kong's unique advantages and strong support from the motherland, as well as its close international connections, both sides can help build the country’s financial strength.

 

Secretary for Financial Services & the Treasury Christopher Hui also attended the meeting. Mr Chan and Mr Hui finished their visit to Beijing and returned to Hong Kong this afternoon.

title: SFST visits Northern Metropolis
body:
Secretary for Financial Services & the Treasury Christopher Hui led a delegation of local financial sector representatives to the Northern Metropolis today to review its construction progress. The delegation comprised senior management from the asset management, private equity, insurance, accounting and fintech sectors, alongside representatives from financial regulatory bodies.

 

The group visited the Hong Kong-Shenzhen Innovation & Technology Park, the Kwu Tung North New Development Area (NDA), and the Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen NDA. This itinerary allowed them to examine local industrial layouts and assess future investment and financing opportunities. 

 

Through these on-site inspections, delegates gained a comprehensive understanding of the development advantages of "one river, two banks" and "one zone, two parks" in the Hetao Shenzhen-Hong Kong Science & Technology Innovation Co-operation Zone and its synergy with the San Tin Technopole. They also observed the emerging infrastructure in the Kwu Tung North NDA and reviewed Hung Shui Kiu/Ha Tsuen’s proximity to Qianhai as a professional services and logistics hub.
 

Discussions also focused on how financial services can support technological innovation and meet the substantial project financing needs driven by Kwu Tung Station, the Northern Link, and local housing plans. The delegation also explored potential the commercial potential of the Hung Shui Kiu Industrial Park, large-scale district developments, and the upcoming University Town.

 

Mr Hui noted that the Chief Executive explicitly highlighted finance as Hong Kong's fundamental strength in the recently announced First Five-Year Plan. He described the Northern Metropolis as the ideal setting to realise the “dual integration” of a “Finance+” strategy with the real economy, positioning the financial sector as an active engine driving strategic transformation.

 

“We organised this visit precisely to enable the financial industry to have the first-hand insights into the land, with a view to comprehensively promoting the integrated development of the financial sector and the real economy,” Mr Hui stated. He added that leveraging market forces and social capital to secure sustainable financial support for local infrastructure, commercial projects, and industry parks remains a key strategy for the Government.

 

“This is also the most vivid embodiment of our full-fledged efforts to drive Hong Kong's evolution from a 'financial city' into a 'finance-empowered city', using finance as a catalyst to boost development in technology, green transition and livelihoods,” he noted.  

 

To support this vision, the Financial Services & the Treasury Bureau and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority are exploring options within the regulatory capital framework for banks to facilitate financing for government-related entities, such as park companies and funded universities. This measure aims to unlock greater financing flexibility to accelerate projects in the area.

 

Furthermore, following updates to the risk-based capital regime for the insurance industry, preferential capital treatment will be introduced for infrastructure investments from December 31 this year. The Government anticipates that this new measure will drive substantial insurance capital into infrastructure projects across the Northern Metropolis development.

title: Govt issues 4th digital green bonds
body:
The Government today announced the successful pricing of around HK$20 billion worth of digital green bonds denominated in HK dollars (HKD), Renminbi, US dollars and euros under its Sustainable Bond Programme. 

 

The issuance has once again set a new record for the largest digital bond issuance in the world.

 

It also reinforced the Government's commitment to promoting innovation in the bond market.

 

Alongside traditional settlement rails and the tokenised central bank money option introduced in the previous issuance, tokenised deposits, empowered by EnsembleTX, were incorporated into the primary issuance settlement process for the HKD tranche of this issuance.

 

It represented the world's first digital bond that integrates tokenised deposits in HKD, advancing towards a more integrated digital ecosystem, and laying a foundation for exploring the programmable features of digital money.

 

This issuance also continued to advance adoption of global standards. By adopting the International Capital Market Association's latest Bond Data Taxonomy Version 2.0, the issuance promoted greater data consistency, interoperability and end-to-end automation across the bond lifecycle.

 

Financial Secretary Paul Chan said the Government has successfully issued digital green bonds for the fourth time, totalling HK$20 billion, which is the largest issuance of its kind globally.

 

He highlighted that the offering was oversubscribed, demonstrating strong market appetite for tokenised products issued in Hong Kong.

 

Mr Chan also noted that these bonds, denominated in multiple currencies, cater to the asset diversification needs of both local and overseas investors, and have incorporated a range of innovative technologies to further advance innovation in the bond market.

 

“The Government will continue to issue tokenised bonds on a regular basis, expand the use cases for the underlying technologies, and harness fintech to empower the bond market's continued development," he added.

 

Secretary for Financial Services & the Treasury Christopher Hui said this issuance demonstrated the Government's ongoing commitment to supporting innovative forms of bond issuance and driving green transformation.

 

He added that it will also further enhance society's understanding of the integration of sustainable development and fintech, while strengthening Hong Kong's position as a leading global green and sustainable finance hub.

title: HK’s innovation index ranking rises
body:
Hong Kong's ranking rose by one place to 14th globally among 139 economies and remained 5th in Asia in the Global Innovation Index 2026 published by the World Intellectual Property Organization today.

 

As regards the two sub-indices under the index, Hong Kong's ranking in the "Innovation Input" sub-index remained at 8th globally, while its ranking in the "Innovation Output" sub-index rose by one place to 21st.

 

The Government said that it is pleased to see the good progress Hong Kong has achieved in the index, highlighting that expediting the development of innovation and technology (I&T) has been a policy priority.

 

The Government also noted that it is fully committed to developing Hong Kong into an international I&T centre, following the directions set out in Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan.

 

Hong Kong will enhance the institutional framework for I&T development, expedite alignment with key national strategies in technology, and develop the new "three major I&T parks and five key research and development institutions" paradigm.

 

The city will also advance new industrialisation accordingly to establish a framework with Hong Kong characteristics for a new industrialisation system, as well as take forward the AI+ Initiative on all fronts by enhancing the layout of computing infrastructure, supporting small and medium-sized enterprises in accelerating their adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), and empowering different sectors of the economy through AI technology.

 

Meanwhile, Hong Kong will leverage the advantage of being closely connected to the Mainland and the world to develop an international hub for science and technology co-operation, as well as deepen the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, thereby attracting global I&T resources and talent.

 

The Government emphasised that it will strive to realise the vision in the Five-Year Plan that Hong Kong will essentially establish an international I&T centre based in the bay area, serving the entire country, while connecting to the world, after 2030.
